name: ATLAS
tagline: Config-driven controls testing and reporting platform for 50+ payment apps
note: Public-level view. The code is internal to Citi: no app names, systems, people or internal figures here. The proposal comes from my USF ISM 6417 papers.

children.title: Inputs
children.summary: Everything arrives as files: payment extracts from 50+ apps, risk and control reports, and reference data.
children.detail: Today the data layer is shared folders, so each cycle starts with collecting files. The newest file in each folder is detected automatically.

children.title: Payment extracts
children.summary: Monthly transaction files from each payment application in the testing program.

children.title: Risk + control reports
children.summary: Weekly risk, control, issue and assessment extracts that feed the MCA pipelines.
children.detail: Ten large report files are read in parallel each week.

children.title: Reference data
children.summary: Approval-threshold matrices, staff directory with approver grades, client and business mappings.

children.title: Prior snapshots
children.summary: Last week's outputs, so every run can show what is new, carried over or resolved.

children.title: Newest-file detection
children.summary: Finds the latest Excel/CSV in each input folder so nobody has to rename files.

children.title: Config layer
children.summary: Each app is a JSON entry plus two template scripts, so adding an app doesn't touch platform code.
children.detail: Business rules and per-app settings live in config instead of being hard-coded. A hot-reload endpoint picks up config changes without a restart.

children.title: One entry per app
children.summary: Name, folders, test types and rules per application, registered in one config file.

children.title: Processing + validation templates
children.summary: Every app gets a processing script and a validation script started from a template.

children.title: Column remaps
children.summary: When a source renames a column, the fix is a one-line remap in JSON, not new code.

children.title: Hot reload
children.summary: Reload config without restarting, behind two layers of auth.

children.title: Cleaning layers
children.summary: Raw files go through ingest, standardize, validate, transform and output layers, like bronze to silver to gold.
children.detail: Same input plus same rules gives the same output every time. Record counts are logged at every step so a drop can be traced to the exact step.

children.title: 1 · Ingest
children.summary: Reads big Excel files fast (Rust-backed reader, parallel threads) and caches them to Parquet.
children.detail: A same-day rerun skips the re-read.

children.title: 2 · Standardize
children.summary: Renames columns, splits IDs, converts amounts to USD, normalizes business names and status values.

children.title: 3 · Validate
children.summary: Fails fast on missing required columns; catches bad amounts that would silently turn into zero.
children.detail: That zero-amount check came from a real bug: formatted amounts were coerced to 0 and under-flagged high-value payments.

children.title: 4 · Dedupe + keys
children.summary: Removes duplicate records and builds derived keys so sources can be joined safely.

children.title: 5 · Join + enrich
children.summary: Left joins controls to issues and mappings, then adds risk categories and flags.
children.detail: Swapping a first-match lookup for a proper left join fixed issues being understated by about 30%.

children.title: 6 · Scope filters
children.summary: Keeps only in-scope payments: value-date window, app scope and exclusion rules.

children.title: 7 · Output + reset
children.summary: Writes CSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON and ZIP, then clears caches so stale data never leaks into next week.
children.detail: Parquet files come out about 60-70% smaller than the Excel originals.

children.title: Rules engine
children.summary: Applies each control's business rules to the full population of payments, not a sample.
children.detail: The team designed the controls; ATLAS runs them on every payment, every month, on top of the manual monthly samples.

children.title: Approval threshold
children.summary: Large payments need an approver with a high enough grade, checked against each app's own matrix.

children.title: Duplicate payment
children.summary: Every potential duplicate (same amount, payee, date, originator) must be released or cancelled.

children.title: Dual blind rekey
children.summary: Two people key the same payment; mismatch rates map to pass, review or fail bands.

children.title: Control effectiveness
children.summary: Rates each control effective or deficient from testing results, open issues and loss events.

children.title: Projected flips
children.summary: Finds the single issues that, once fixed, would flip a control back to effective.

children.title: Weeks-to-target forecast
children.summary: Projects when a business reaches its effectiveness target from its week-over-week pace.

children.title: Pipelines
children.summary: 37 registered pipelines, each its own script set, run from one orchestrator.

children.title: Payment control tests
children.summary: Threshold, duplicate and rekey testing across the payment apps, rolled into a monthly matrix.

children.title: MCA weekly snapshot
children.summary: Replaced 17 undocumented Power Query steps with an 11-step Python pipeline.
children.detail: Ran side by side with the old process and was reconciled row by row before cutover.

children.title: Remediation forecast
children.summary: Weekly Polars pipeline: snapshot, classify issues, project effectiveness, diff vs last week, build decks.

children.title: Threshold analysis
children.summary: Cross-app threshold analysis written out as a set of CSV reports.

children.title: Rekey trends
children.summary: Monthly trend report that classifies rekey mismatches by type.

children.title: Payment KPI metrics
children.summary: Monthly payment KPI pipeline that chains many scripts into one run.

children.title: Staff utilities
children.summary: Consolidates staff data used for approver checks.

children.title: Orchestrator
children.summary: A Flask web app where you click Run and watch the pipeline's logs stream live.
children.detail: Each run is a separate subprocess, so one failing pipeline can't take down the app.

children.title: App factory + blueprints
children.summary: Flask app factory with blueprints and a service layer (script, chart, data services).

children.title: Run API
children.summary: Run, cancel and status endpoints per app.

children.title: Subprocess isolation
children.summary: Processing then validation run as child processes, isolated from the web app.

children.title: Live logs
children.summary: Socket.IO streams start, log, finish and result events to the browser as the run happens.

children.title: Watchdog
children.summary: Checks the server every few minutes and restarts it if it stops.

children.title: Login
children.summary: The dashboard sits behind authentication on the internal network.

children.title: Dashboards
children.summary: Several live dashboards on top of the pipeline outputs, plus decks for senior managers.

children.title: Script orchestrator
children.summary: Cards for every pipeline with Input, Output and Run buttons, grouped by category.

children.title: MCA dashboard
children.summary: Effective vs deficient, risk tiers, deficiency drivers, trends and a week-over-week comparison.

children.title: KPI analytics
children.summary: Payment KPI trends over monthly snapshots.

children.title: Threshold dashboard
children.summary: Threshold test results and review across apps.

children.title: Staff consolidation
children.summary: Staff and approver data in one view.

children.title: Weekly HTML decks
children.summary: Self-contained decks per business and bank-wide, built automatically every week.

children.title: Outputs
children.summary: Each consumer gets the format it needs: Excel for analysts, Parquet for code, JSON for dashboards.

children.title: Test evidence
children.summary: Monthly matrix and exception lists used as control-testing evidence.

children.title: Historical trends
children.summary: Monthly consolidated outputs kept as history for trend reporting.

children.title: Audit logs
children.summary: Run logs kept alongside outputs.

children.title: New / carried / resolved
children.summary: Week-over-week diff of issues on a stable key.

children.title: Testing + quality
children.summary: Production-grade: pipelines have pytest suites and were reconciled against the old process before cutover.

children.title: pytest suites
children.summary: The remediation forecast alone has 112 tests, including regression tests for every bug fixed.

children.title: Parallel run
children.summary: Old and new processes ran side by side for weeks; final row counts had to match the inputs.

children.title: Count logging
children.summary: Record counts at every step, added after a trailing-space bug hid rows from a filter.

children.title: AI-assisted dev
children.summary: GitHub Copilot used daily to write and test Python.

children.title: Managed data platform
children.summary: Replace shared folders with a governed historical data layer the team can query, not just files.
children.detail: The foundation everything else depends on. Requirements first, then pick the technology (database, warehouse or lakehouse).

children.title: Controlled ingestion
children.summary: Pull from source systems on a schedule instead of requesting and moving files by hand.

children.title: Data contracts
children.summary: Each source documents schema, owner, frequency, IDs and allowed values.

children.title: Validation layer
children.summary: Check required fields, types, allowed values, keys and duplicates before any transform runs.

children.title: Bronze → silver → gold
children.summary: Raw, cleaned and business-ready layers with historical snapshots and stable IDs.

children.title: Lineage + catalog
children.summary: Trace any number back to its source file, transform step, rule version and period.

children.title: Business-rule registry
children.summary: Rules move out of prompts and people's heads into versioned config.

children.title: AI layer
children.summary: Code calculates and validates every number first; AI explains it and answers questions about it.
children.detail: Deterministic systems set the facts, ML finds patterns, generative AI explains, and people keep the decisions.

children.title: Executive insight layer
children.summary: AI gets validated metrics and biggest movements and writes the commentary. No more spreadsheet math in a chat.

children.title: History Q&A assistant
children.summary: Turns a question into a controlled query over the history layer, then explains the answer.
children.detail: Answers follow-up questions in the meeting instead of sending the team back to the files.

children.title: Policy RAG assistant
children.summary: Combines the factual result with the current policy or control definition, retrieved with owner, version and date.

children.title: Anomaly triage
children.summary: Statistics and unsupervised ML flag unusual control behavior; AI summarizes why; a person decides.

children.title: MCP access channel
children.summary: Models reach data only through governed tool connections that respect permissions.

children.title: Security + governance
children.summary: AI inherits access rules instead of going around them, and every data activity has one owner.

children.title: SSO + role-based access
children.summary: Company sign-in, least-privilege roles and data classification.

children.title: No leak through retrieval
children.summary: If you can't open a dataset or policy, the assistant can't show it to you either.

children.title: RACI + data owners
children.summary: Named owners and stewards; the person doing a change isn't the only one signing off.

children.title: Quality SLAs
children.summary: A measurable 'good enough' per dataset, close to 100% for anything regulator-facing.

children.title: Secrets vault
children.summary: Credentials move into a managed secrets store.

children.title: Human accountability
children.summary: Material risk calls stay with qualified people; AI output is never the final decision.

children.title: Ops at scale
children.summary: Scheduled, parallel, monitored and deployed through CI/CD instead of clicked by hand.

children.title: Scheduling + run history
children.summary: Pipelines run on a schedule with a run-history table and pre-flight checks.

children.title: Workers + DAGs
children.summary: Parallel workers and dependency-aware DAGs with retries and alerts.

children.title: Notifications
children.summary: Exception lists and run results pushed to the team automatically.

children.title: Containers + CI/CD
children.summary: Containerized deploys with automated tests gating every change.

children.title: Monitoring
children.summary: Central logs and dashboards for pipeline health.

children.title: Phased rollout
children.summary: Level by level: prove each layer before the next one is allowed to depend on it.

children.title: 1 · Document + reproduce
children.summary: Data dictionary, source catalog and runbooks; rebuild the current process deterministically.

children.title: 2 · Reconcile
children.summary: Match the old outputs on a representative period until they agree.

children.title: 3 · Automate reporting
children.summary: Deterministic reporting on the managed layer.

children.title: 4 · AI explains
children.summary: Add AI commentary and Q&A on validated results.

children.title: 5 · RAG + anomaly ML
children.summary: Then policy retrieval and anomaly detection, with model governance.
